benchmark_name: DepressionAgent: Reading, Listening, Seeing, and Deliberating Multimodal Evidence for Depression Risk Assessment
institutions: Shenzhen MSU-BIT University (Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Joint Laboratory for Emotional Intelligence and Pervasive Computing; Artificial Intelligence Research Institute); The University of Hong Kong; Tsinghua University
ground_truth_source: Dataset-defined binary depression risk labels from D-Vlog and LMVD public benchmarks; ground-truth labels accessed only after inference for metric computation
what_assessed_skills: Multimodal depression risk assessment via explicit evidence deliberation: modality-specific evidence extraction (text, audio, video); support–challenge reasoning; cross-modal arbitration; conflict reflection; risk-sensitive textual reassessment; explainability/inspectability of reasoning
tasks_assessed: Binary depression risk classification (depressed vs. not depressed) from multimodal video data; multimodal evidence extraction and deliberation; cross-modal conflict resolution; risk reflection for false-negative reduction
population_represented: YouTube vloggers (D-Vlog: 816 speakers, English vlogs); social media video participants (LMVD: 1,475 participants, multiple platforms); real-world unconstrained environments
evaluation_method: Automated evaluation on benchmark test sets using Accuracy, Precision, Recall, and F1-score (positive class = depression risk); ablation studies; reflection transition analysis; language masking experiments. Human evaluation by 5 clinicians (2 junior, 3 senior psychiatrists) on 30 D-Vlog samples using 5-point Likert scale (Evidence Relevance, Reasoning Coherence, Clinical Utility) and binary reasonable/unreasonable judgments for structured reasoning operations; ICC and Fleiss' κ for inter-rater agreement. Evaluation: Both (Automated + Human).
performance_scores: D-Vlog (matched test set): Acc=95.26%, Prec=95.24%, Rec=96.15%, F1=95.69%. LMVD (matched test set): Acc=82.57%, Prec=80.48%, Rec=85.76%, F1=83.04%. Full D-Vlog pool: Acc=92.43%, F1=93.20%. Cross-model accuracy gains vs. direct prediction: Qwen3-Omni +20.1pp, GPT-5.5 +29.1pp, Gemini 3.1 Pro +20.7pp. Clinician Likert means: Evidence Relevance=3.65, Reasoning Coherence=3.71, Clinical Utility=3.21.
short_summary: DepressionAgent is an evidence-centric, reflection-driven multi-agent framework for multimodal depression risk assessment from text, audio, and video. Rather than fusing latent features, it explicitly extracts modality-specific evidence, organizes it into self-report and audio-visual behavioral branches with Hypothesis and Challenger agents, performs cross-modal arbitration with Conflict Reflection, and applies Risk Reflection for low-risk cases to reduce false negatives. The framework operates in a zero-shot, training-free setting using LLMs (default: Qwen3-Omni-30B-A3B-Instruct) and is evaluated on D-Vlog and LMVD benchmarks. It achieves state-of-the-art competitive performance (95.69% F1 on D-Vlog test set) and is additionally assessed by five clinicians for reasoning quality and inspectability.
